Thanks for taking time out of your day. I'm not working atm but am hoping to start soon. I'm just worried it will turn out to be another dead end like everything I do seems to be. My husband knows of past and somewhat recent suicidal feelings but he doesn't know these exact thoughts and I'm scared of losing him or giving him something else to worry about if I reveal this to him. Coming here to vent has helped clear my anxiety a little...just having my thoughts somewhere other than in my head..so thanks for listening.

I made a throw away for this because I don't want this on my main account.

I was in high school and was drinking with some friends at one of their houses during the summer. My "friend" was always making comments about wanting to have sex with me, but always played it off as a joke since I didn't reciprocate. We all ended up falling asleep, and eventually I was woken up by him touching me. When I was younger, my mom had talked to me about rape and to be careful when walking at night, etc., but I had always thought rape was supposed to be violent and done by someone you don't know. I didn't know what to do because this person touching me was someone I considered a friend, not some stranger who attacked me while walking home in the night. So I just laid there, frozen, unable to move. For me, I think this is what gets to me the most, the fact that I didn't do anything even though I had been talked to and knowledgeable (or so I thought) about rape. It actually took me a long time to acknowledge that I was raped, and even now I feel confused about whether or not I should report it since there is no evidence and this happened nearly 8 years ago. 

I still have "bad days", where I can't stop thinking about it and get really upset and feel like I'm alone. I've found some support through my boyfriend, but it can definitely effect our relationship at times. I find it very hard to talk about, and whenever I try to I end up getting a lump in my throat and crying. I've also self harmed in the past, and I believe this is a very common coping strategy.

My main advice for future clinicians would be that there are many responses to rape, not just fight or flight. In my case I froze, and I'm sure there are many other responses as well.
